Released at 2026-10-21

* SECURITY: **Go 1.27.3, which fixes GO-2026-6809 (`crypto/x509`) that govulncheck reports.** Go 1.27.2 ships a `crypto/x509` that trusts compromised intermediate certificates, and govulncheck finds it reachable from the S3 client paths (for example `manifest.Manifest.LoadFrom`). Both go.mod files, `go.work`, the three Dockerfiles and the parity runner image now use Go 1.27.3. `govulncheck` reports no vulnerabilities in either module. No source change; Parquet data is unchanged.

* FEATURE: **Deletes: a tombstone is a write-once object that every pod reads from the bucket.** The definition (and, for a `hide` delete that is undone, an `.undo` object) is created once with `If-None-Match` under `{prefix}_tombstones/`; every pod lists new keys each minute and enforces them, so a delete reaches all pods within a minute instead of at the next restart, and nothing a pod holds locally ever causes a DELETE. While `delete.enabled` is true, a pod that cannot refresh its list for three minutes answers cold and buffer-bridge reads with `503` (an undecodable definition closes only the tenants it names), and a select pod is ready only after its first sync. Only a `hide` delete can be un-deleted; `permanent` and `auto` hide the rows like `hide` and answer `409` to an un-delete, because physical removal is not enabled in this release ([#627](https://github.com/ReliablyObserve/victoria-lakehouse/issues/627)); `delete.default_mode` now defaults to `hide` (it was `auto`), also for upstream's `run_task`: the bytes stay until retention and direct Parquet readers still see them. `active_tasks` is `[]` and `stop_task` a no-op, as for a finished upstream task. Key times are pod clocks (late keys are counted: `LakehouseTombstoneClockSkew`). New: `lakehouse_delete_tombstone_view_age_seconds`, `LakehouseTombstoneViewStale`, `LakehouseTombstoneUnreadable`. See `docs/deletion-strategy.md`.
* FEATURE: removed: **The mutable tombstone protocol and everything built on it:** the per-tombstone record, its disk and S3 write-through, the delete rewriter and scheduler, the leftovers API (`GET /delete/logsql/leftovers`, `/delete/tracessql/leftovers`), their metrics and alerts, and the unread knobs `delete.auto_rewrite_classes`, `delete.rewrite_delay`, `delete.rewrite_max_concurrent`, `delete.verify_interval`. **Upgrade note: tombstones written by an earlier release (`_tombstones/<id>.json`) no longer hide rows and are not migrated; they are rejected without error and counted each hour in `lakehouse_delete_tombstone_keys_rejected_total`. Re-issue those deletes, and remove the old objects by hand.**

* BUGFIX: **The compacted layer of the all-column sort parity case no longer leaves an object unmerged (tests only, no behaviour change, [#636](https://github.com/ReliablyObserve/victoria-lakehouse/issues/636)).** The forced compaction merges only the objects the segment guard releases when it runs, and the case triggered it as soon as two objects per tenant were released; a batch that a segment seal cut into two segments left its later object at L0, which failed the layer proof and the restart layer after it. The case now waits until the guard releases every object of its tenants and requires the trigger to merge them all, and it writes its second batch in two segments on every run, for both binaries.
* BUGFIX: **The span events and links parity cases no longer wait up to 12 minutes for the next hour (tests only, no behaviour change).** From minute 48 of an hour, `TestParity_Traces_EventsLinksLayers` and `TestParity_Traces_EventsLinksInvalidUTF8` slept until the next hour before writing their spans, so that a run never crossed an hour boundary. The span time is now the current time, moved by at most 2 s so that every timestamp of a case (span starts and ends, trace index rows, the second batch) falls in one hour partition; this also closes a first-second-of-the-hour window in which the old rule split a case over two partitions. The rest of the case already derives its partition from the span time, and its layer proofs are unchanged.
